preconditions.description: The number of cities n and queries q are within the specified bounds.

preconditions.expression: len(a) == n and all(1 <= x <= n for x in a)
preconditions.description: The mineral resource list a has exactly n elements, each between 1 and n.

preconditions.expression: len(edges) == n - 1 and all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n and u != v for u, v in edges)
preconditions.description: There are exactly n-1 edges, each connecting two distinct valid cities.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n and 1 <= l <= r <= n for u, v, l, r in queries)
preconditions.description: Each query specifies valid city indices and a valid range [l, r].
The given edges form a valid tree structure connecting all n cities.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly q lines, one for each query.

postconditions.expression: all((int(line) == -1) or (l <= int(line) <= r and is_odd_count_on_path(u, v, int(line), tree, a)) for line, (u, v, l, r) in zip(output_lines, queries))
postconditions.description: For each query, the output is either -1 (indicating no solution) or a valid mineral resource c such that l <= c <= r and c appears an odd number of times on the unique path between u and v.

postconditions.expression: all((int(line) == -1) == (not any(l <= c <= r and is_odd_count_on_path(u, v, c, tree, a) for c in range(1, n + 1))) for line, (u, v, l, r) in zip(output_lines, queries))
postconditions.description: The output is -1 if and only if no mineral resource in the range [l, r] appears an odd number of times on the path between u and v.
